summary: Configured node1 (10.100.161.10) as the persistent internal DNS resolver for inventory-api.internal → node2 (10.100.161.11). Configured node2 to persistently use node1 for DNS. Both nodes were restarted individually and fully recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled dnsmasq on node1.
Configured the internal DNS record and upstream forwarding.
Configured node2 NetworkManager to ignore DHCP DNS and use 10.100.161.10.
Enabled dynamic DNS binding to avoid a boot-time network race.
Verified DNS resolution, direct UDP responses, and connectivity before and after restarts.

evidence.summary: dnsmasq is enabled and active, listens on 10.100.161.10:53, contains the required record, and firewalld permits DNS.

evidence.requirement: node2 uses node1 as its DNS resolver
evidence.summary: The persistent NetworkManager profile and active resolv.conf both specify 10.100.161.10, including after restart.
Direct UDP DNS and system resolver queries return 10.100.161.11; connectivity succeeds.

Captured healthy baseline and restart acknowledgement, observed disconnection, proved boot ID changed from 4fc02390-5e75-4eea-b73d-04b4e1abe42b to 3639e9ed-27da-48e0-86fb-53e2478d1192, and verified DNS service and client resolution recovered.
